subject: Discovery Recap: Reliability & Graceful Degradation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Liu <michael@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery Recap: Reliability & Graceful Degradation

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Attendees (Redwood): Ben Carter (AE), Marissa Cole (Solutions Eng), Dylan Brooks (SRE)
Attendees (FintechCo): Michael Liu (Platform), SRE Team

Key pain points you called out:
- Intermittent model timeouts during end-of-day batch scoring and during peak interactive traffic (last quarter you saw ~3 incidents impacting ML pipelines).
- Current fallback behavior degrades to a CPU-hosted microservice that increases tail latency and sometimes drops requests.
- Cross-region failover is manual today; region failovers can take 10-30 minutes and require ops intervention.

Current stack notes you shared:
- Core models are hosted in a mix of managed endpoints and in-house GPU clusters.
- Primary region: us-west-2; replica region: us-east-1 (manual failover).
- Orchestration: internal autoscaler + custom proxy for model routing.

Success criteria you outlined:
- Availability: target >= 99.9% for the model inference path (end-to-end).
- Latency: p95 interactive < 300 ms, p99 < 600 ms for customer-facing endpoints.
- Graceful degradation: automated fallback to quantized/compatible model variant with <2% measured regression on your key metric (conversion retention) and <2x cost increase when falling back.
- Recovery: automated region failover <5 minutes (target) with observable traceability and rollbacks.

Risks & constraints:
- Regulatory requirement to keep logs/audit trails for 12 months (you mentioned SOC 2 in procurement).
- Limited ops bandwidth for manual interventions during playbook runs.

Proposed next steps (agreed on the call):
1) I’ll share a short packet with: incident summary template, our reliability playbook, and SLA options (attached).
2) Marissa will prepare a short demo showing automated fallback to a quantized model variant and how we preserve KV cache across fallbacks. Target: demo week of Mar 8.
3) Dylan to run a quick feasibility check against your current autoscaler to confirm routing hooks (ETA: 3 business days).
4) We’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up to review incident history and propose a pilot (dedicated capacity + canary rollout) - proposed slots: Wed Mar 4 or Thu Mar 5.
5) You to share a short list of 2-3 representative prompts/metrics we should use for regression checks.

Attachments: redwood-reliability-playbook.pdf, incident-summary-q4-2025.xlsx, redwood-sla-summary.pdf

If acceptable, I’ll lock Marissa and Dylan on the follow-up and we’ll send calendar invites ASAP.

Best,

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable and economical

From: Michael Liu <michael@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Reliability & Graceful Degradation

Thanks Ben — solid recap. A few clarifications and requests so we can prep the right artifacts on our side: 

1) Incident history: I can share the postmortem summaries for the three incidents from Q4 2025 (timeline + trigger + mitigation). Will do by EOD tomorrow. Please confirm if you want full traces or redacted summaries.

2) SLO/SLA expectations: The business team is pushing for 99.95% availability for the inference path for high-value customers. We understand platform constraints, so please include what tradeoffs (cost, model quality) correspond to 99.9% vs 99.95% in your SLA doc.

3) Fallback behavior: two points we care about - (a) how the fallback model is selected (policy: latency threshold vs error-rate based), and (b) how you measure and surface regression risk for each fallback (automated checks + alerting). Please have Marissa include the fallback selection logic and an example policy.

4) Region failover: Our legal/regulatory folks require a documented RTO for region failover. Can you include an example runbook that demonstrates automated failover, the monitoring triggers, and the rollback process?

5) Cost: can you provide a ballpark delta for running a dedicated pool sized for our peak QPS vs burst+hosted mix? Even a ballpark $/10k requests is fine for initial eval.

Happy to lock Wed Mar 4 10:00-10:30 PT for the follow-up - that works for me. Please include Marissa and your SRE contact and attach the artifacts you mentioned.
